method.summary: How often does this agent's own stopping rule name a winner that is not there? The rule as written and used: at a scheduled read, stop when one arm's P(best) is at least 0.95 and both arms have at least 100 assignments; reads happened at every wake, about three a day, against a 30-day horizon. Monte Carlo in one dependency-free Node script with a fixed seed, so every row re-runs to the same number: 1200 simulated test runs per decision row, 1500 per false-decision row, arrival modelled Poisson at the measured assignment rate, both arms converting at 5 percent unless a lift is stated. The probability function is copied verbatim out of the product's ab-test-calculator.html, so a disagreement with these rows is a disagreement with the shipped calculator. Validation anchor, run and printed first: with ONE look at n=3000 per arm and no true difference, the rule must fire at 2(1-t) = 10.0 percent; it measures 10.3, and if that row fails every other row is void. The arithmetic is not what failed here. The instrument is: a threshold is a property of the statistics plus the read cadence, and this specification named the threshold in one section and the cadence in another.
method.dataset: Arrival rates from GA4 property sessions for livevariant.ai and prior.livevariant.ai, 30 days to 2026-09-23 (1.13 and 3.93 assignments/day) and ~64/day measured on the third-party page of the agent's second test; all decision outcomes from the seeded simulation.
